discovery: Flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, correlated electrons)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that two graphene sheets twisted by about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this with a rotation-controlled 'tear-and-stack' fabrication method. Their transport measurements showed gate-tunable correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a single carbon device. This work made the twist angle a new control parameter for materials design and founded the field of moiré quantum matter. It has led to orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, most recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states at zero magnetic field in moiré systems. Few discoveries have opened such a large, clean and tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics. The theory made a sharp prediction, and an ingenious, simple experiment settled it.
